record_notes.DCP-LETT-359: Answers Buckland question asked last night in person about Galapagos lizards. Observations are Darwin recollections, not an incoming letter prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-369: Editing instructions to Shoberl friend; FitzRoy agreement follows seeing him. Oral and manuscript context, no surviving incoming letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-380: Acknowledges a publisher rights document: footnote preserves Colburn agreement with FitzRoy. It is a third-party document, not an incoming letter addressed to Darwin. Both September22 and23 remain possible.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-383F: Resumes proof supervision after returning Saturday night; Monday October23 inferred from itinerary. No individual incoming request identified.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-422: Requests a future meeting about shells; Sowerby is in town. Does not respond to a surviving note, and Friday August-December window stays unresolved.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-429: Sulivan report from Falklands includes weather, geology, sections and intended later soundings. His book is with his father. May describe earlier joint discussions, not a located letter from Darwin; composition is not Darwin receipt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-458: Official Geological Society thanks for Proceedings volumes. Institutional formula signed by Darwin; publication donation is the object, no accompanying letter identified.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-488: Explicitly delayed answer to an unlocated Broderip note about shells and mould. Separate questions to Owen and discussion of moles do not identify an extant input.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-511: Official thanks for Proceedings volume1 number6. No incoming covering letter established.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-511A: Official thanks for Mantell geological specimens donated May22; letter written May23. Specimen-donation date is not a letter receipt date.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-518: Buckland acknowledges Journal received June7. No surviving covering Darwin letter identified; book acknowledgement alone is not a direct pair.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-531: Publisher manuscript assessment with anonymity request. Plans August24 departure although itinerary records August23; future plan and actual event differ, not necessarily a dating error.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-547: Sends specimens for Eyton examination after an undertaking and accepts offered game birds. Medium of undertaking unproved; no incoming letter matched. Preserve tabular specimen structure and earlier Journal references.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-13770H: Valediction-only scrap with conjectured Leighton recipient and 1840-1877 date range. Source attribution and period remain held.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-549: Delayed response to missing Eyton letter about bird descriptions, drawings and bones. Birth last Friday week supports January6 chronology; earlier outgoing547 is not the missing prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-566: Sulivan answers missing Darwin request for curvature/dip calculations; Darwin used old Falmouth address. Mathematical tables require layout preservation. Later May12 input cannot explain Darwin February letter555.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-641A: Received unidentified Murchison paper yesterday and answers probable Buckland enquiry about Dugard. Maps are an earlier gift, not a surviving cover letter. Broad November1840-February1841 Wednesday retained.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-584: Explicitly acknowledges unlocated membership election letter. Membership event and December1 response are secure; no invented input.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-631: XML selects July1-23,1841, but editorial note explicitly allows Shrewsbury visits from summer1841 to November1848. Preserve raw safe classification and add a conservative editorial period hold, plus diagram/location evidence. No certain1841 persona grounding.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-640: Delayed answer to unlocated Broderip note; requested Bell answer has not arrived because Bell departed before the enquiry. House purchase remains subject to conveyancer opinion.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-671A: Answers unlocated Mantell letter requesting help for his son. Promises to pass it to FitzRoy, who Darwin has not seen for eight months. Missing incoming is shared with later676; outgoing671A cannot itself prompt676.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-675: Long incoming fragment answers unlocated Darwin animal and geological questions. Main body begins and ends incompletely; paragraphs31-39 are separate postscripts whose association is only probable. Date May10 is based on Darwin annotation, not demonstrated delivery. Preserve diagrams, prior-season observations and conditional specimen dispatch.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-676: Reports FitzRoy has now read Mantell original letter and retained it; fulfils promise in671A. Both surviving letters are Darwin-authored: reject Luna direct-reply arrow between them. Original Mantell input remains missing.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-680: Same unlocated Dieffenbach translation note received July4 is reported to Colburn and acknowledged in680A. Requests plate permission. This is a useful shared missing-source route, not a surviving incoming pair.
